best_for: Households and small businesses who want real double-entry books on their own computer, with no subscription and no bank-linked cloud service.
description:
GnuCash is personal and small-business accounting software, written, documented and translated entirely by volunteers. Its menus come in 61 languages.

You enter money in a register that looks like a checkbook, with split transactions, autofill and cleared or reconciled marks. Reconcile an account against your bank statement to catch missing entries and typos. Accounts can be in different currencies, and stock and fund prices can be pulled from the web to update your portfolio. A small business can track customers, vendors, jobs, invoices and bills, and even run payroll. There is a guided setup for mortgage and loan payments, and you can print checks on common check stock.

points.title: Double-entry, the proper way
points.text: Every transaction moves money between two accounts, so the books balance and errors show up. It takes more thought than a simple budget app, and it gives you reports an accountant will recognize.

points.title: Bank data mostly by file
points.text: GnuCash imports QIF, OFX, CSV, CAMT and SWIFT MT9xx files and matches them against what you already entered. Direct online banking goes through FinTS and AqBanking, which mostly suits banks that support those standards; elsewhere, plan on downloading statements yourself.

points.title: Stocks and small business too
points.text: It tracks stock, bond and mutual fund accounts, runs scheduled transactions, and has small-business accounting, reports, graphs and financial calculators.

points.title: Free, with no account
points.text: GnuCash is open source under the GPL 2.0 or later. Your data stays in a file on your computer. The homepage mentions no mobile app.

points.title: Version 5.17 needs a newer OS
points.text: 5.17 runs on Windows 8, 10 and 11, macOS 11 or later on Apple silicon, and macOS 10.13 or later on Intel. Version 3.11 is the last for Windows 7 and macOS 10.12, and 2.6.21 the last for Windows XP and Vista.

points.title: Windows build is 32-bit
points.text: The Windows installer listed here is a 32-bit build that installs for all users, so it needs administrator rights. The Windows listing keeps 31 versions; macOS and Linux list only the current release.

points.title: Linux Flatpak is official
points.text: The Flatpak on Flathub is published by the GnuCash project and marked verified, for x64 and Arm64. Distribution packages also exist but may trail the latest release.
